evidence.claim: Generac’s August 2025 investor presentation described a large and growing data-center opportunity, a global supply shortfall for large diesel generators, and data-center product backlog above $150 million as of July 30, 2025.
Generac highlighted competitive lead times, global generator assembly capability, service network support, and focus on backup power generation as competitive positioning for data centers.

Broadwind’s 2025 10-K says its Gearing segment serves power generation and provides gearbox repair, loose gearing, gearboxes, precision machining, and heat-treat services for aftermarket and OEM applications.

Broadwind’s 2025 10-K states that its Industrial Solutions segment provides supply-chain solutions, inventory management, kitting, and assembly services primarily serving the combined-cycle natural-gas turbine market.

If gas-turbine and power-island manufacturing slots become constrained, Broadwind could be a second-order beneficiary through kitting, controls-related assemblies, valve assemblies, sensor devices, fuel-system components, electrical junction boxes, and electromechanical devices; materiality remains unverified.

memory_update.text: CAT should be retained as a reference leader for large reciprocating engines, Solar Turbines, prime-power orders, and data-center speed-to-power validation, but not treated as the alpha-discovery focus.

GNRC is a direct underfollowed-to-medium-attention candidate because the market may still frame it as residential outage exposure while data-center large-megawatt generator backlog and service-network capacity are becoming more relevant.

BWEN is a speculative-shadow micro-cap exception: its 10-K confirms gas-turbine and power-generation supply-chain exposure, but the next layer must prove revenue materiality and customer/order evidence.

Later Layer 1B passes should check Cummins, GE Vernova, Siemens Energy ADR/foreign listing, Mitsubishi Heavy ADR/foreign listing, Woodward, Chart Industries, emissions-control suppliers, turbine controls, and MRO/service tooling names.

node: Gas turbines, turbine services, reciprocating engines, backup generation, and power-island equipment
summary: Layer 1B expands the dispatchable-generation power-island node with one obvious leader/context anchor and two discovery-lane names. The node appears tied to speed-to-power for AI/data-center loads, with evidence strongest for large reciprocating generator sets and backup-power systems. Underfollowed exposure is harder to prove: Broadwind is a speculative micro-cap supplier into combined-cycle gas-turbine and power-generation component chains, but customer concentration and segment mix require later verification.
